en: Vādhūla Śrautasūtra 1.1–1.4 [Agnnyādheya, Punarādheya].
The extent covered by each manuscript is as follows: K1, K2, M, C: 1.1.1.1–1.4.4.33 [= End].
T2 serves as a variant reading for T1 from 1.1.3.11 through 1.4.4.33 [the end].
[Note: -ṁ represents the *anunāsika*; -;h represents the *upadhmānīya*. For 1.1.1, the manuscripts utilized are K1, K2, M, H, and C.]

1.1.1.1 One who is about to establish the sacred fires (agnīn) should collect the following materials: saline earth, sand, mole-hills, earth dug up by boars, the mound of an anthill, gravel, a lotus leaf, six pieces of gold, and a hundred-māna weight of gold—these are the earthly materials; the wood of the *aśvattha* and the *audumbara*—these are the wooden materials; the wood of the *pālāśa*, the *śamī*, the *vaikaṅkata*, wood struck by lightning, and wood from the heart of a *śamī* tree; twenty moist fuel-sticks with their leaves from a marked *aśvattha* tree; a horse; and all the sacrificial implements (*yajñāyudha*).
1.1.1.2 Three [fires] are to be dug out. 1.1.1.3 On the day of the fast (upavasatha), one should indeed prepare food; one may even cook a cow, provided that one has a calf.

1.1.1.4 Regarding the ritual investigation of the establishment of the sacred fires (agnyādheya): one who desires spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) should fetch fire from the house of a Brāhmaṇa who performs many sacrifices; one who desires sensory power (*indriya*) should fetch it from the house of a Rājanya; one who desires prosperity (*puṣṭi*) should fetch it from the house of a Vaiśya who possesses much livestock.
1.1.1.5 If he should obtain this [desired] object, having fetched the fire two or three days beforehand, he should kindle it as his domestic fire (āmātya).
1.1.1.6 Having removed it in the afternoon, he places it upon the spot where the Anvāhāryapacana fire is to be established.
1.1.1.7 He gives that [fire] to the ancestors.

1.1.1.8 “May Agni hear my call with the fuel-stick!”—with this [verse], having offered four spoonfuls upon a bunch of *darbha* grass placed on the excavated site of the Gārhapatya fire, he throws down a piece of gold and offers the *anu-vitti* oblation with: “May the Waters and the divine Dhiṣaṇās hear my call, svāhā!
1.1.1.9 In the same manner, he offers on the excavated site of the Āhavanīya fire.
1.1.1.10 Having covered themselves, they return after this oblation.

1.1.1.11 They pour this fire into a vessel. 1.1.1.12 He pours it out upon the excavated site of the Gārhapatya fire. 1.1.1.13 He pours down for him the wood-shavings with which he has kindled it during that night.
1.1.1.14 At the time when the sun is above the trees, he prepares the *brahmaudana* (the Brahmin’s rice-mess) with [the formula]: "By the impulse of the god...

1.1.2.1 “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I pour out [the grain] acceptable to Aditi, acceptable to the Ādityas,” [saying this, he pours out] four cups of rice.
1.1.2.2 Having poured water into those same four [cups], he places them on the cooking pot. 1.1.2.3 On a red hide, they pound the *brahmaudana* (the Brahmin’s porridge).

1.1.2.4 When it has been cooked, he causes it to be poured out; he scrapes the hollows from the cooking pot, but not from the embers. 1.1.2.5 He spreads clarified butter and a piece of gold in a vessel.
1.1.2.6 He draws out three ladlefuls, each with a base-layer and a sprinkling of butter over it.
1.1.2.7 Having then drawn up [the milk] upwards as much as desired, having spread it out, and having thrown in a piece of gold, he pours [water] over it profusely.
1.1.2.8 Four *ārṣeya* priests consume that.
1.1.2.9 The sacrificer himself should wash them; thus [it is said].
1.1.2.10 The Adhvaryu instructs them: "Having eaten once, throw it up. Having eaten once, they throw it up.

1.1.2.11 With the verse, "Worship Agni with fuel," he pours out the *brahmaudana* (the Brahman’s rice-mess) right here and places fuel-sticks upon the fire with *gāyatrī* verses, [reciting]: "Awaken the guest with clarified butter; offer the oblations into him, svāhā!
1.1.2.12 The exclamation *svāhā* is used for all the fuel-sticks.

1.1.2.13 “*Upa tvāgne haviṣmatīr ghṛtācīḥ = samidho mama svāhā, tan tvā samidbhir aṅgira bṛhac chocā yaviṣṭhya svāhā*”—thus [he says]. 1.1.2.14 Having poured out [the remainder] around, he sets down the clarified butter. 1.1.2.15 From this point onward, those who have partaken of the *brahmaudana* eat twice.
1.1.2.16 He gives a pair [of animals] at the *samit* offerings, and an *āṇḍīvala* fish at the *brahmaudana* according to his faith, for the purpose of eating from the cooking pot.
1.1.2.17 He says, "Instruct the sacrificer," [to which the other replies], "That which is to be instructed by you. 1.1.2.18 He instructs whatever is to be instructed by him.

1.1.2.19 He causes the debt to be transferred either to his son or to his brother. 1.1.2.20 At the time for the *nipadas*, he places the two fire-drills (*araṇī*) before him with the words: "You two are possessed of the season. [He says: "O you two who have Agni as seed, conceive an embryo! On this day I have taken you two; that is the truth, that you shall support a hero and shall give birth to a hero.
1.1.2.21 Thereafter, he restrains his speech.

1.1.2.22 Restraining his speech, he kindles the fire with wood-shavings throughout the night; he should indeed remain awake, for he must not sleep, and he should remain under her control. 1.1.2.23 With the verse, “O Jātavedas, the seed of the world,” he heats the two kindling-sticks (*araṇī*) while reciting: “Pour here [the seed] from austerity, that which shall be born as Agni, the bearer of oblations, from the *aśvattha* tree; generating him from the womb of the *śamī* tree, who is the source of bliss.
1.1.2.E With the verse, “This is your seasonal womb,” he causes the fire to ascend into the two kindling-sticks.
1.1.3.1 With the words, "This is your seasonal womb," he causes the fire to ascend into the two kindling woods with the verse, "From whence born... having ascended, increase our wealth."
1.1.3.2 They pour this fire into a vessel. 1.1.3.3 Its flame is produced by friction.
1.1.3.4 Once it has been born, they carry this fire from the site where the Anvāhāryapacana fire was dug out.

1.1.3.5. Having sprinkled [the materials] with water, he takes the fire into himself with two verses: "I take Agni first into myself... and "...for the increase of wealth, for good offspring, for heroic vigor—do not depart. 1.1.3.6.
With the verse, "Those bodies of yours which are dear," he mixes the ritual materials (sambhāra), [reciting]: "May your dear hearts be united; [unite] my bodies with yours. 1.1.3.7.
Over the ritual materials, he causes the Hotṛ priests to recite.

1.1.3.8. With the formula, "I spread the *ṛta* as soil upon the earth," he pours down the third of the ritual materials (*sambhārāḥ*) on the excavated site of the Gārhapatya fire. 1.1.3.9. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Upon *ṛta* I establish truth; upon truth I establish Agni. 1.1.3.10.

Having sprinkled [the wood], he takes up a chip [of wood] with the formula, "Thou art the birthplace of Agni"; [he takes] the two friction-sticks with "Ye two are the testicles"; the lower friction-stick with "Thou art Urvaśī"; and the upper friction-stick with "Purūravas. He anoints them with the formula, "Anointed with ghee"; he places them together with the formula, "Do ye two provide the testicles."
"Be born after the *gāyatrī* metre"—with these words he turns himself toward himself by means of the metres; "be born after the *triṣṭubh* metre, be born after the *jagatī* metre.
He recites the *daśahotṛ* formula over the two kindling woods;
they churn the fire.
1.1.3.14 He consecrates the newborn with the mantra: "Thou art life.
1.1.3.15 Upon the birth [of the child], he releases his speech, saying: "I grant a boon.
1.1.3.16 He places the child in his joined palms with the three syllables: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ."
1.1.3.17 “O lord of vows, I establish you with the vow of these gods,” [he says] according to whichever deity [the sacrificer] belongs to.
1.1.3.18 “With the Gāyatrī metre,” [says] a Brāhmaṇa; “with the Triṣṭubh metre,” [says] a Rājanya; “with the Jagatī metre,” [says] a Vaiśya.

1.1.3.19 “I breathe upon you with the breath of Prajāpati,” he says, breathing upon him; “with the nourishment of Pūṣan, for my long life, for a hundred autumns, for a hundred autumns of life, for splendor.”

1.1.3.20. While seated to the south, the Adhvaryu throws a piece of gold to the north [of the student] with the words: "O Ordainer, bestow prosperity upon me. 1.1.3.21. He makes him recite: "Make me the overlord of prosperity; may Indra, the generous lord of the quarters, anoint me with glory. I abandon exhaustion, lack of food, and disease; unite with my dear body. 1.1.3.E.
With the words, "I have become one like you," he worships the [fire] while sitting down.

1.1.4.1 He worships the cow that is lying down with the mantra: "I am from you"—"You are me; this is mine; you are my womb, I am your womb; carry the oblations to the gods each to their proper place, O son, world-maker Jātavedas.

1.1.4.2 He worships with the three verses beginning with "This spotted bull has stepped forth," including the verse containing the word *prajāpati* (the sovereign), ending with: "He has found his mother again and his father, going toward heaven; the mighty bull [has gone] to the thirtyfold heaven."

1.1.4.3 At the Gārhapatya fire, which overcomes the oblations, he offers the oblation of the Daśahotṛ with [the ladle] filled four times. 1.1.4.4 He worships with the Rathantara [Sāman], [saying]: "We cry out to thee, O Hero, like unmilked cows; O Indra, Lord of this moving world, beholder of heaven, Lord of that which stands still, O Indra—no other like thee exists, neither celestial nor terrestrial; none has been born, nor shall be born; none has been born, nor shall be born; O bountiful Indra, we, seeking horses and desiring cattle, call upon thee as warriors."
1.1.4.5 They kindle the sacrificial fuel (idhma) and prepare the supporting ladles (upayamanī); they bring the washed horse.
1.1.4.6 They wait for the rising sun with the Āhavanīya fire.

1.1.4.7—When the sun has risen, he lifts up the fuel with three verses: "For vigor and strength, I lift thee up"; "Thou art the subduer of rivals, the slayer of Vṛtra for the manly, roaring, long-lived one, for splendor. That greatness of thine among the gods which leads to heaven, that soul of thine which has entered into cattle, that nourishment of thine which has spread among men—with that, O Agni, come to us graciously from heaven, from earth, from the intermediate space, from the wind, from Parjanya, and from the plants; wherever thou hast been born, O Jātavedas, from there, O Agni, come to us graciously."

1.1.4.8. With the verse, "Go forth toward the eastern quarter, O wise one," they set out with the horse leading. With the verse, "O Agni, be the fire before Agni here for all... for the two-footed and four-footed," 1.1.4.9. they arrive at the *viṣuvat* (midday) point. Standing there, he says, 1.1.4.10. "Spread the ritual materials (*sambhāra*) of the *anvāhāryapacana* fire.
With the formula, "I spread the *ṛta*, the soil upon the earth," he pours half of the ritual materials onto the excavated site of the *anvāhāryapacana* fire.
1.1.4.11 He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "From the Truth I take up the Untruth; from the Mother I take up Mātariśvan, Vāyu, and Agni.
1.1.4.12 He says, "Pouring down, [I establish] the fire.
1.1.4.E He consecrates it with the mantra: "The earth by its abundance..."

1.1.5.1 He consecrates it [the fire] with the mantra: "Thou art earth by thy abundance; thou art heaven by thy expanse; thou art the atmosphere by thy greatness. O Goddess Aditi, in thy lap I place Agni, the eater of food, for the sake of eating food.
1.1.5.2 With the words, "O Ordainer, bestow glory upon me," the Adhvaryu, seated to the south, throws a piece of gold to the north of him.

1.1.5.3 He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Make me the overlord for prosperity; may the ruling Maghavan Indra anoint me with glory. I leave behind exhaustion, lack of food, and disease; unite with my dear body.

1.1.5.4 At the midpoint, he worships a piece of gold placed there with the verse: "May these riches attend upon me. He worships with: "May I dwell here together with these offspring; let the great one stand firm, possessing all forms. Shine forth, O Jātavedas, in the midst of wealth!"

1.1.5.5 With the verse, “In what way has the wondrous one appeared for us? they proceed beyond the *viṣuvat* with the *vāmadevya* chant: “O ever-increasing friend, with what most powerful host? Which true exhilaration of the soma-draughts shall intoxicate you most richly, so that you may break open even the firmest wealth? Be a protector of us, your friends and singers, with a hundred aids.
1.1.5.6 He causes the horse to step forward toward the east, from the north, at the footprint of the southern shoulder for the sake of the oblation.
1.1.5.7 Again, he causes it to step backward with that same [foot].
1.1.5.8 He releases it toward the north.

1.1.5.9 With the words, "I spread the *ṛta* as soil upon the earth," he pours the ritual materials (*sambhāra*) over the oblation. 1.1.5.10 He causes [the sacrificer] to recite, "Upon *ṛta* I establish truth; upon truth, Mātariśvan; I establish Sūrya and Agni"; thus he completes the *yajus*.
1.1.5.11 He pours down the supporting sands (upayamanī).

1.1.5.12 He settles the Āhavanīya fire with all five [formulas], beginning with "bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar. 1.1.5.13 With the formula, "By the vow of those gods, O Lord of Vows, I establish thee," he establishes it according to the deity to whom [the sacrificer] belongs: "with the Gāyatrī metre," for a Brāhmaṇa; "with the Triṣṭubh metre," for a Rājanya; "with the Jagatī metre," for a Vaiśya.

1.1.5.14. With the words, "O Ordainer, bestow prosperity upon me," the Adhvaryu, sitting to the south, throws a piece of gold to the north [of him]. 1.1.5.15. He makes [the sacrificer] recite: "Make me the overlord of prosperity; may Indra, the Maghavan, the lord of the quarters, anoint me with glory. I leave behind exhaustion, lack of food, and disease; unite with my dear body."

1.1.5.16 He worships the six [fires] with the verse: "That which here [is] in heaven... and "Those two waters, being in agreement, came into being there above the earth; upon them Jātavedas was placed, bringing welfare to offspring and comfort to the body.

1.1.5.17 He says, "Bring the clarified butter (ājya). They bring two portions of clarified butter: that which has been scooped out and that which remains in the butter-pot. 1.2.1 He says, "Bring the clarified butter. They bring two portions of clarified butter: that which has been scooped out and that which remains in the butter-pot.

1.2.1.1. With the verses beginning "The first law is indeed being kindled," he places the fuel-sticks (*samidh*) on the fire using *triṣṭubh* meters, having anointed them with clarified butter (*ājya*). [He offers: "He is anointed with ointments, the one who possesses all boons, whose hair is flame, whose garment is clarified butter, the purifier, the excellent sacrificer—Agni, for the sacrifice of the gods, Svāhā! Whatever fuel-sticks there are of yours, O Agni, those which are on the earth, on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), or in the sun—may they go to this oblation of clarified butter for the god-devoted sacrificer, granting him protection, Svāhā! Seven...

"O Agni, these seven tongues of yours are fuel-sticks; the seven Ṛṣis, the seven dear abodes, and the seven *hotṛ*-priests worship you in seven ways. Fill the seven wombs with clarified butter—*svāhā*!
(1.2.1.2) With [the ladle] filled four times, he offers to the Saptahotṛ [formula] into the Āhavanīya fire.

1.2.1.3 He worships with the *bṛhat* [sāman]: "For we indeed invoke thee, O singer, for the winning of booty; thee, O Indra, lord of the virtuous, men invoke in battles against the Vṛtras; thee in the races of the steed, thee in the races of the steed. As such, O wonderful one, wielder of the thunderbolt, mayest thou be bold toward us when praised, O lord of the stone; when praised, O lord of the stone, pour forth for us cattle and horses for the chariot, O Indra, like a conqueror ever victorious."

1.2.1.4. Having gone around the Gārhapatya fire by its western side with the verse, "Thee, O Agni, being kindled, O youngest one," he places the fuel sticks upon it with *jagatī* verses, having first anointed them with the remaining clarified butter. On the Anvāhāryapacana fire, [he offers] with the verses: "The gods have made thee their messenger, the bearer of oblations, wide-striding, whose womb is clarified butter; when invoked, they have established thee as a brilliant eye that impels the sacrifice, Svāhā! Thee, O Agni, from of old invoked with clarified butter, those seeking favor have kindled with excellent fuel; growing strong and nourished by the plants..."

"Thou spreadest thy wide strides over the earthly realms, Svāhā! Agni, whose face is ghee, whose source is ghee, kindled by ghee—ghee is his food. The rivers carry thee, dripping with ghee. Drinking the ghee, O God, thou sacrificest to the gods, Svāhā!
(1.2.1.5) With [the oblation] taken four times, he offers to the *Ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula on the *Anvāhāryapacana* fire.

1.2.1.6 He worships with the *vāravantīya* chant: "Like a horse that wins the prize, [I worship] thee... and "Let him honor Agni with prostrations, the sovereign lord of sacrifices; may he, our son, wide-striding in his might, the very gracious one, be bountiful to us; as one who possesses all life, protect us always from the malevolent mortal, both from afar and from near at hand.
1.2.1.7 He offers the *pañcahotṛ* formula in the domestic chamber and the *caturhotṛ* formula in the assembly hall.

1.2.1.8 Having arrived, he worships them all with the *śyaita* [sāman], beginning with the verse: "O bounteous ones, come hither... and [the hymn] "Praise Indra, as is known, the Maghavan who is the foremost treasure for his singers; he bestows gifts as if by the thousands, he bestows gifts as if by the thousands; like one with a hundred armies, he moves forth boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the donor, he slays the Vṛtras for the donor; like the streams from a mountain, his gifts overflow, the gifts that nourish many.
1.2.1.9 He performs [the rite] together with the head. With the words, "The Gharma is the head," he worships the Gārhapatya fire.

1.2.2 1.2.2.1 He worships the *gārhapatya* fire with the words: “The heat (*gharma*) is the head; may this Agni become well-pleased with the cattle; grant protection to our children and descendants. With the words: “The wind (*vāta*) is the breath,” he worships the *anvāhāryapacana* fire: “May this Agni become well-pleased with the cattle; cook well-pleasing food for our children and descendants. With the words: “The sun (*arka*) is the eye,” he worships the *āhavanīya* fire: “That is yonder sun; may this Agni become well-pleased with the cattle.”

1.2.2.2 He says, "O bright one, that bright luster of yours... [and] over the Āhavanīya fire itself: "The bright body, the bright light, the unaging; with that shine for me, with that I establish you. O Agni, by means of Agni and the *brahman*, I have attained; I have pervaded; I have pervaded a full lifespan. 1.2.2.3 He places [fuel sticks] upon the Virāj [fire], having anointed them all around with water: "O Agni, those two auspicious bodies of yours... [and] two [sticks] upon the Gārhapatya: "The Virāj and the Svarāj—may they enter me, may they quicken me; with these two I establish you, Svāhā!"

1.2.2.4. With the two verses beginning, “O Agni, those two auspicious bodies of yours,” he addresses the Anvāhāryapacana fire: “May Samrāj and Abhibhū enter me; may they quicken me; with them I establish you, svāhā! 1.2.2.5.

With the two verses beginning, “O Agni, those two auspicious bodies of yours,” he addresses the Āhavanīya fire: “May Vibhū and Paribhū enter me; may they quicken me; with them I establish you, svāhā!”

1.2.2.6. With the two verses, "O Agni, those two auspicious bodies of yours," he places [fuel] specifically on the Āhavanīya fire with the formula: "May *Prabhvī* and *Prabhūti* enter me; may they quicken me; for them I establish you, svāhā! 1.2.2.7.

He adds fuel for the *Pavamāna* body, having anointed it with the residue of the butter, with one verse: "O Agni, that *Pavamāna* body of yours which has entered into the earth, which is in the *Gāyatrī* metre and in the *Rathantara* Sāman—for that I establish you; svāhā to it! [He does so] on the Gārhapatya fire.

1.2.2.8. With the verse, "O Agni, that purifying body of yours," he recites one [verse] over the Anvāhāryapacana fire: "That which has entered into the intermediate space, that which is in the Triṣṭubh metre, that which is in the Vāmadevya Sāman—with that I establish you; to that body of yours, Svāhā! 1.2.2.9. With the verse, "O Agni, that bright body of yours," he recites one [verse] over the Āhavanīya fire: "That which has entered into heaven, that which is in the Jagatī metre, that which is in the Bṛhat Sāman—with that I establish you; to that body of yours, Svāhā!"

1.2.2.10 Taking a vessel of water and going out toward this direction—the east and the north—he worships with the verses recited in the forest regarding his own bodies, and whatever the sacrificer hates, that he meditates upon.
1.2.2.11 Having sprinkled water around [the fire], he returns without looking back.

1.2.2.12 Having arrived, he worships with the *virāj* meters: "O manly one (*narya*), protect my offspring"—thus the *gārhapatya*; "O Atharvan, protect my food (*pitum*)"—thus the *anvāhāryapacana*; "O reciter (*śaṃsya*), protect my cattle"—thus the *āhavanīya*; "O expansive one (*sapratha*), protect my assembly (*sabhām*)"—thus the *sabhyam*; "O deep-seated one (*budhniya*), protect my mantra"—thus the *āvasathīya*.
1.2.2.13 From here on, he offers the *pūrṇāhuti* (full-offering). 1.2.2.14 Having enclosed [the fire-places], he takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter for the *āhavanīya*.
1.2.2.15 Having filled [the vessel], he recites the *saptahotṛ* formula; he places this verse, "Seven are yours," in the middle.
1.2.2.16 Having laid on a fuel-stick, he offers with the oblation of the *hotṛ*.
1.2.2.17 He grants him a boon.
The *pūrṇāhuti* concludes; from this point on,
he performs the *agnihotra*.
1.2.3.1 Thereafter, he indeed offers the Agnihotra. 1.2.3.2 When [the milk] has been drawn out, he recites the Daśahotṛ formula.
1.2.3.3 With "bhūḥ svāhā," he offers the first oblation; with the Hotṛ's oblation, [he offers] the subsequent one.
1.2.3.4 He now pays homage to the fires.
1.2.3.5 With the verse, "Going forward to the sacrifice," he addresses the Āhavanīya fire; with the verse, "Let us speak a prayer to Agni, who hears us from afar," [he addresses the same].
1.2.3.6 With the verse, "Following his ancient splendor," he addresses the Gārhapatya fire; with the verse, "The bold ones milked the bright milk from the seer who wins a thousandfold."
1.2.3.7 He worships the Āhavanīya fire with the verse, “Agni is the head—[he quickens the seeds from the height of heaven].

1.2.3.8 [He worships] the Gārhapatya fire with the verse, “This one was first established here by the establishers—[the Hotṛ, most skilled in sacrifice at the ritual, for the sake of the people]. 1.2.3.9 He worships both together with the verse, “Both of you, Indra and Agni, I invoke—[both of you, I call upon for wealth, for gain]. 1.2.3.10 [He worships them] with the verse, “[Both of you, I call upon for gain, for gain].”
1.2.3.10 He worships the Āhavanīya fire with [the verse]: "This is your seasonal womb; from whence born... increase our wealth.

1.2.3.11 With the two verses addressed to Agni-Pavamāna, beginning with "O Agni, you purify our lives," he worships the Gārhapatya fire, [concluding] with: "Bring us strength and food; bestow upon me prosperity and wealth.

1.2.3.12 With the two verses beginning with "O purifying Agni, with your light," he worships the Anvāhāryapacana fire, [concluding] with: "With your pleasant tongue, O God, bring the gods... and our oblation."

1.2.3.13 With the two verses beginning, "Agni, whose vows are most pure," he worships the Āhavanīya fire with [the verse], "Pure, O sage... do thou honor the lights. 1.2.3.14 [He worships] the Āhavanīya itself with [the formulas]: "O Agni, you are the giver of life; give me life," and "O Agni, you are the giver of splendor; give me splendor; protect my body; fill up for me what is deficient.
1.2.3.15 With the formula, "O Citrāvasu, may I reach your end in safety," he meditates upon the night mentally.
1.2.3.16 He places a fuel-stick [on the fire] with: "Kindling thee for a hundred winters," and [concludes] with: "Radiant, may we kindle thee; full of vigor, upon the highest vault—*svāhā*!

1.2.3.17 He worships [the fire] with: "O Agni, thou hast attained the splendor of the sun," and [concludes] with: "Be united with the praise of the *ṛṣis*; create [us] with offspring! 1.2.3.18 He says: "May they establish thee as their own, O sacrificer"; [therefore] one should meditate on that which is otherwise in the mind.
1.2.3.19 He consecrates that which has been prepared with the mantra:
"I behold all the offspring, the human ones, rich in food; may they all be in our house. You are water; may you become abundant for me. (1.2.4.1)
1.2.4.2 With the words, "Thou art the Saṃhitā, possessing all forms," he touches the calf of the Agnihotra cow; [and with] "May the strength and abundance come to me; may your riches rest upon me.

1.2.4.3 With the three *gāyatrī* verses beginning, "To thee, O Agni, day by day," he worships the Āhavanīya fire; [with] "O dispeller of darkness, through our prayer, homage... do thou attend us for our well-being.

1.2.4.4 With the three two-footed verses beginning, "O Agni, thou art our nearest [kinsman]," he worships the Gārhapatya fire; [with] "And be a protector, auspicious and a refuge... most brilliant, grant us wealth."

1.2.4.5. With the words, "With strength I look upon you; with strength look upon me," he gazes at the houses. 1.2.4.6. With the words, "With the abundance of wealth I look upon you; with the abundance of wealth look upon me," [he gazes] at the cattle. 1.2.4.7.

With the words, "You are the *iḍā*s, the honey-makers," he addresses those very [cows]; then, "Enter me gently, O you who bring delight; may I thrive through a thousandfold prosperity; may your riches rest within me."
1.2.4.8 He recites "That excellent splendor of Savitṛ" over the Āhavanīya fire, and "May the radiance of the god impel us.
1.2.4.9 He recites "The Soma, the one who makes us hear" over the Gārhapatya fire, and "Make [him] like Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij, O Brahmaṇaspati.
1.2.4.10 He recites "Never art thou barren" over the Āhavanīya fire, and "O Indra, thou dost not fail the worshiper; may the prayer of the god be united."

1.2.4.11 With the *anuṣṭubh* verse, "O Agni, we [take] thee as a fortress... (*pari tvāgne puram vayam*), he approaches the *gārhapatya* fire, [reciting] "...the sage, O powerful one, [protect us] from the treacherous" (*vipraṃ sahasya bhaṅgurāvata*).

1.2.4.12 With the words, "O Agni, lord of the house" (*agne gṛhapate*), he pays homage, [saying]: "May I be a good lord of the house through thee as lord of the house; may thou be a good lord of the house through me as lord of the house. 1.2.4.13 He invokes blessings, [saying]: "A hundred winters—this blessing I invoke for myself and for so-and-so, [may it be] full of light. First he mentions his own name, [and then says] "for so-and-so, for so-and-so."
1.2.4.14. [The offering] for the sons [is performed] in successive order, ending with the word "threads" (tantavaḥ).
From this point on, it is indeed the preparation of the oblation (haviṣkḷpti).
1.3.1.2 Having arranged the sacrificial implements and having led forward the waters, he offers a cake on eight potsherds to Agni.
1.3.1.3 He performs the *tanū* oblations. 1.3.1.4 Once the offering has been set out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* verses and the *pṛśni* verses.
1.3.1.5 When [the fire] has drawn near, he recites the *apānagrahas* and the *pṛśnis*.
1.3.1.6 Having touched [the fire] while reciting, "The draft-animals have settled; that which is mine, O Agni," he recites the *daśahotṛ* formula.
1.3.1.7 He says the invitatory verse for the fire being kindled.
1.3.1.8 He recites seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses. 1.3.1.9 While invoking [the deities], he invokes them including the *tanū* [verses]: "Agni Pavamāna, then Agni, then Agni Pāvaka, then Agni Śuci.
1.3.1.10 When the *sāmidhenīs* have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* spoon, he says: "O *Āgnīdh*, cleanse the fires three times each!"

1.3.1.11 Having stepped across without letting the two *sruks* touch each other, having anointed the *dhurva*-pole and set them down, he chooses the *pravara*. The *hotṛ* sits down; being impelled, he takes up the two *srucs*.
1.3.1.12 He performs the *prayāja* offerings.
1.3.1.13 Having performed the *prayājas*, having stepped across, he pours clarified butter twice over the *dhruvā*; once over the oblation, and twice over the *dhruvā* last of all.
1.3.1.14 He offers the two portions of clarified butter (*ājyabhāgau*); [these are] the two *ājyabhāgas* that slay Vṛtra.

1.3.1.15 Saying, "Recite for Agni Pavamāna," while taking four portions of clarified butter, he recites after [the invitatory verse]: "O Agni, thou purifiest the lives... and he offers with the offering verse: "O Agni, purify yourself. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation.

1.3.1.16 Saying, "Recite for Agni," while spreading [the base] and cutting [the portion], he recites after [the invitatory verse]: "Agni is the head... and he offers with the offering verse: "Thee, O Agni, from the lotus... When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation.

1.3.1.17 “Recite for Agni Pāvaka,” he says, taking four portions of clarified butter. He recites the invitatory verse, “O Agni Pāvaka, with thy light...”; he offers the oblation with the offering verse, “Do thou, O purifier, shine for us...,” and pours it when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered. 1.3.1.18 “Recite for Agni Śuci,” he says, taking four portions of clarified butter. He recites the invitatory verse, “Agni, whose vows are most pure...”; he offers the oblation with the offering verse, “Upward, O Agni, thy pure [flames]...,” and pours it when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered. 1.3.1.19 “Recite for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt,” he says, spreading [butter] twice.
1.3.1.20 He cuts a single portion from the northern half of the sacrificial cake and pours clarified butter over it four times.
1.3.1.21 The *sviṣṭakṛt* offering consists of seven portions.

1.3.1.22 The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *gāyatrī* meter; he recites the invitatory verse, "O Agni, be awakened by the hymn," and he offers the oblation with the offering verse, "He is the bearer of the oblations. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the libation.
1.3.1.23 Having stepped across and set down the two offering-spoons (*srucau*) in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion.
1.3.1.24 Having touched water, he spreads an under-layer of butter three times for the *iḍā*, cuts off [the portions] twice, and pours butter over them five times.
This is the ten-fold *iḍā*.
1.3.1.26 When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [the *prāśitra*] for the *āgnīdh*.
1.3.1.27 They consume it, they sprinkle themselves with water, and they carry it around.
1.3.1.28 When the *prāśitra* has been consumed by the *brahman*, the *āgnīdh* sits down at the rubbish heap (*utkara*) with a water-pot.

1.3.1.29 Here he gives the sacrificial fee for the establishment of the sacred fires (agnyādheya). 1.3.1.30 He offers the oblation following the continuity of the Hotṛ. 1.3.1.31 The rite is successfully accomplished; this sacrifice comes to a conclusion.
1.3.1.32 Having arranged the sacrificial implements and having led forward the waters, he offers a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra and Agni.
1.3.2.1 He offers a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra and Agni, and a pap to Āditya. 1.3.2.2 Once it has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.
1.3.2.3 When [the oblation] has been placed near, he recites the *apānagraha* formulas, the *pṛśni* verses, and the *daśahotṛ* formula.
1.3.2.4 For this [offering], the two butter-portions (ājyabhāga) contain the word *vṛdhant*. 1.3.2.5 He says, "Recite for Indra and Agni," while spreading [the base] and cutting [the portion].
1.3.2.6 He recites, "O Indra and Agni, the luminous realms of heaven," and he offers with the words, "He struck down Vṛtra"; at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the oblation.

1.3.2.7. "Recite for the Ādityas," he says, while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion]. 1.3.2.8. He recites, "May Aditi protect us," and he offers with the verse, "The great mother..."; when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the oblation. 1.3.2.9. The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
1.3.2.10 He offers the oblation following the continuity of the Hotṛ’s [recitation]. 1.3.2.11 The rite succeeds; this sacrifice is concluded.
1.3.2.12 This, then, is the Dvibarhis [sacrifice].

1.3.2.13 Now, if he should perform the *tribarhis* [rite], having set out the sacrificial implements (*yajñāyudha*) and having carried forth the waters, he offers a cake on eight potsherds (*aṣṭākapāla*) to Agni and a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pavamāna. 1.3.2.14 This first oblation is entirely composed of *gāyatrī* verses. Having set out the sacrificial implements and having carried forth the waters, he offers a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pāvaka and a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Śuci.
1.3.2.16 For this [offering], there are two butter-portions (ājyabhāga) rich in wealth; for the two oblations, [there are portions] according to the respective deities.
1.3.2.17 The two Virāj verses are the concluding offerings (saṃyājyā).
1.3.2.18 He offers the oblation following the continuity of the Hotṛ’s recitation.

1.3.2.19 The rite is accomplished; this sacrifice comes to a conclusion. 1.3.2.20 Having set out the sacrificial implements and having led forward the waters, he offers a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra and Agni, and a pap to Āditya.
1.3.2.21 Thus, this sacrifice is indeed prepared in this manner.
1.3.2.22 This [is] the three-barhis [sacrifice]. 1.3.2.23 But the two-barhis [sacrifice] is established [as follows]. 1.3.2.24 For him, these fires remain kindled for twelve days.

1.3.2.25 This is his vow: he does not speak untruth, he does not eat meat, he does not approach a woman, they do not wash his garment with alkaline salt, he sleeps on the ground, he drinks from a vessel that is not made of clay, he does not consume the remnants of food left by a Śūdra, and he washes his own feet. 1.3.2.26 "He should eat only what is given as alms"—this is one view. 1.3.2.27 "He should observe the vow of consuming only the remnants of the *agnihotra* offering"—this is another view.
1.3.2.28. "Whatever remains of the four ladles that have been poured out shall be his *vrata* (fasting food)"—this is one view.
1.3.2.29. "Whatever may come to him [as food] shall be his *vrata*"—this is another view.
1.3.2.30. Of these, he may do whichever he desires.
1.3.2.31 This is the perpetual attendance upon these fires: "O Agni, [be] full of light.
1.3.3.1 “O Agni, full of light, may I, full of light, kindle thee,” with these words he kindles the Āhavanīya fire; “For the mind, for the world of heaven, thee,” with these words he worships it.
1.3.3.2 “O Agni, full of life, may I, full of life, kindle thee,” with these words he kindles the Gārhapatya fire; “For life, for procreation, thee,” with these words he worships it.

1.3.3.3 He kindles the Anvāhāryapacana fire with the formula: "O Agni, eater of food, I kindle thee, the eater of food. He pays homage to it with the formula: "For breath, for the eating of food. 1.3.3.4 With the formula: "For desire, for pervasion, may I be able, ye luminous ones," he pays homage to all [the fires] together. With the formula: "And protect my wealth and my hope," 1.3.3.5 With the formula:

"May the seers who have become gods protect me," he pays homage to the Seven Seers. With the formula: "And may the immortal bestowers of bodies attend upon us mortals; may the fathers dwelling in heaven enter into me," [he pays homage].
1.3.3.6 Then [he says], "O waters, bearers of vows, may you maintain my vow; in the waters is faith"—with these words, he does not sip water.
1.3.3.7 He covers [the water] with the formula, "Thou art sight, thou art hearing.
1.3.3.8 With the formula, "The immortal Brahman extends five steps," he strides toward the altar.
1.3.3.9. With the three verses beginning, "O Waters, you are indeed sources of bliss," they sprinkle themselves within the altar-ground (*antarvedi*).

1.3.3.10. With the words, "Thou art the dwelling-place of *Iḍā*," he touches this [earth], saying, "May I become the dwelling-place; thou art the foundation, may I find a firm foundation. 1.3.3.11. With the words, "Upon the summit of the ruddy one, I seat myself," he sits down to the south of the *Āhavanīya* fire.

1.3.3.12. "O you who abide in desire, look upon us with desire," with these words he looks at the fires. 1.3.3.13. "May this desire of mine be fulfilled," with these words he prays for whatever desire he may have. 1.3.3.14. Verily, that desire is fulfilled for him.
1.3.3.E Therefore, it is precisely the undertaking [of the action].
1.3.4.1 The commencement [of the rite] is from this point.
1.3.4.2 "Today is the fast-day of the full moon," [saying this], they remove the ashes of the fires, strew grass around the fires, and perform the ritual form of the fast-day.

1.3.4.3 Having not yet offered the evening *agnihotra*, having melted clarified butter over the *gārhapatya* fire and purified it, having wiped the *sruva* and *sruk* ladles, he goes eastward and takes four portions of butter for the *āhavanīya* fire.
1.3.4.4 He offers that [oblation] with the verse, "Full behind," into the Āhavanīya fire.

1.3.4.5 He takes another fourfold portion; he offers that with the verse, "What the gods assigned to thee," into the Āhavanīya fire itself. 1.3.4.6 Having gone back toward the west, he takes a fourfold portion over half of the Gārhapatya fire.
1.3.4.7 He offers that [oblation] in the *gārhapatya* fire with the verse: "That which the gods bestowed upon you...
1.3.4.8 He takes another fourfold portion; he offers that in the *gārhapatya* itself with the verse: "Full behind...
1.3.4.9 Having gone toward the middle of the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, he takes a fourfold portion.
1.3.4.10 He offers that [oblation] with the verse, "The Ekāṣṭakā... [referring to] the Ekāṣṭakā.
1.3.4.11 Having offered [to] the Ekāṣṭakā, they stay [there].

1.3.4.12 Having offered the morning Agnihotra, having melted the clarified butter over the Gārhapatya fire and purified it, and having cleansed both the dipping-spoon (sruva) and the offering-ladle (sruk), he takes four portions of butter right there.
1.3.4.13 He offers that [oblation] in the Gārhapatya fire with the verse: "That which the gods bestowed upon thee...
1.3.4.14 He takes another fourfold portion; he offers that in the Gārhapatya itself with the verse: "Full behind...
1.3.4.15 Having gone toward the middle of the Anvāhāryapacana fire, he takes a fourfold portion.
1.3.4.16 He offers that with the verse, “The image of the year,” dedicated to Prajāpati.
1.3.4.17 Having gone around behind the Gārhapatya fire and having stepped forward toward the east, he takes four portions of clarified butter for the Āhavanīya fire.
1.3.4.18 He offers that in the Āhavanīya fire with the verse, “Full behind.”
1.3.4.19 Furthermore, he takes four portions [of clarified butter] and offers them in the Āhavanīya fire itself with the verse: "That which the gods have bestowed upon thee...

1.3.4.20 Having arranged the sacrificial implements and led forward the waters, he performs the introductory offering (*ārambhaṇīyā-iṣṭi*): a cake on eleven potsherds for Agni-Viṣṇu, a pap for Sarasvatī, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Sarasvant. 1.3.4.21 Once the oblation has been set out, he recites the *prāṇagrahas* and the *pṛśnis*.

1.3.4.22 Having released his speech with the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviskṛt*), he offers the *caturhotṛ* formula with [an oblation] taken four times into the *āhavanīya* fire. 1.3.4.23 He recites that same formula when [the oblation] has been placed near [the fire]. For this [offering], the two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*) belong to Vṛtrahan. 1.3.4.24 With the oblation [he recites]: "O Agni and Viṣṇu! O Agni and Viṣṇu! Forward for us, O Goddess! From heaven to us! The swelling breast of Sarasvatī, whose ordinance all cattle follow. Thus with the oblation.
1.3.4.25 The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
1.3.4.26 Having given a pair of cattle facing southward, he gives according to his faith.
1.3.4.27 He offers an oblation following the continuity of the *hotṛ*'s [recitation].
1.3.4.28 The rite is accomplished; the Ārambhaṇīyā offering comes to a conclusion.
1.3.4.29 Having arranged the sacrificial implements and having led forward the waters, he performs the sacrifice with the well-known full-moon oblation [the Punarādheya].
1.4.1.1 The materials required for the establishment of the sacred fires (agnyādheya) are well known.

1.4.1.2 Now, furthermore, there are a repaired chariot, a mended garment, a bull that has been set free again, Darbha grass with a hundred stalks, six pieces of gold—of these, three are eight-petaled, and two are bundles of grass.
1.4.1.3 Today is the fast-day for the *ṛddhi*-re-establishment of the fires; they remove the ashes of the fires.
1.4.1.4 He kindles the Gārhapatya fire with wood-shavings.
1.4.1.5. When the sun is above the trees, he pours out the *brahmaudana* (the Brahmin’s rice-mess).
1.4.1.6. While that very [rice] is being cooked, the *adhvaryu* offers the *agnihotra*.
1.4.1.7. Once it is cooked, he causes it to be poured back into the pot; he does not scoop it out from the embers.

1.4.1.8 He spreads a layer of clarified butter and a piece of gold in the vessel, [taking care that] it does not spill over. 1.4.1.9 He draws out three ladlefuls, having spread a base and poured a libation over them.
1.4.1.10 Having drawn out as much as desired from there, having divided it, and having thrown in a piece of gold, he pours much liquid over it so that it does not spill over.
1.4.1.11 Four *ārṣeya*s consume that [remnant].
1.4.1.12 The sacrificer himself should wash them, thus it is said.
1.4.1.13 The *adhvaryu* instructs them: "Having consumed once, throw it up! Having consumed once, they throw it up.
1.4.1.14 One does not place fuel-sticks on this [fire].
1.4.1.15 He gives the *āṇḍīvala* (a type of vessel) for the *brahmaudana*, according to his faith, for the consumption from the cooking-pot.
1.4.1.16 They separate these embers of the Āhavanīya and the Anvāhāryapacana fires.
1.4.1.17 When those two have become extinguished, they then remove their ashes.
1.4.1.18 He says, "Instruct the sacrificer," [meaning] "that which is to be instructed for you.
1.4.1.19 He instructs whatever is to be instructed for him.
1.4.1.20 He causes the debt to be paid either by a son or by a brother.
1.4.1.21 At the time for the *nipadas*, he places the two kindling sticks (*araṇī*) upon him with the words, "You are possessed of the season. 1.4.1.22 Thereafter, he restrains his speech.

1.4.1.23 He maintains silence throughout the night and kindles the fire with wood shavings; he should indeed remain awake and not sleep, and his will should prevail. 1.4.1.24 At dawn, the Adhvaryu places the Agnihotra oblation on the fire.
1.4.1.25 He makes the fuel-stick as thin as possible.
1.4.1.26 He remains seated, restraining his speech, while holding the two kindling woods (*araṇī*). 1.4.1.27 They set two bundles of grass on fire at the sacrificer’s station.
1.4.1.28 They cast the two bundles of grass into the Gārhapatya fire for the Āhavanīya, and into the Āmātya fire for the Anvāhāryapacana.
1.4.1.29 The Adhvaryu runs after [the sacrificer] with the Agnihotra oblation that has been poured out. 1.4.1.30 They set down two bundles of grass.
1.4.1.31 Having placed a fuel-stick and offered the first oblation as if to reach it, he offers the second, larger oblation.
1.4.1.32 When those two have become extinguished, they wipe away their ashes. 1.4.1.33 They fill the two pits with sand.
1.4.1.34 With the verse, "O Jātavedas, the seed of the world," he heats the two fire-drills while moving them back and forth.
1.4.1.35 With the words, "This is your seasonal womb," he causes the fire to ascend into the two kindling woods (araṇīs).
1.4.1.36 They pour this fire into a vessel. 1.4.1.37 At this point, he offers the *anu-vitti* oblation.
The ritual act is accomplished by placing him in one's joined palms.
1.4.2.1 The ritual act is accomplished by placing him [the fire] in the hollowed palms.
1.4.2.2 He places him in the hollowed palms with the three syllables: "bhuvo bhūr.

1.4.2.3 With the formula, "O Lord of Vows, I place you here by the vow of these gods," he uses whichever deity's name applies; "by the Gāyatrī metre," for a Brāhmaṇa; "by the Triṣṭubh metre," for a Rājanya; "by the Jagatī metre," for a Vaiśya.
1.4.2.4. With the words, “By the breath of Prajāpati, I breathe upon you,” he breathes upon him.

1.4.2.5. With the words, “O Ordainer, bestow glory upon me,” the Adhvaryu, sitting to his south, throws down a piece of gold weighing eight *pṛḍa*s to his north. 1.4.2.6. He makes him recite: “Make me the overlord of glory; may Indra, the lord of the quarters and possessor of wealth, anoint me with fame. I abandon exhaustion, lack of food, and disease; unite with my dear body.”
1.4.2.7 He worships the seated [fire] with the verse, "Today I am from you.
1.4.2.8 He worships with the three verses of Sarparājñī beginning, "This spotted cow has stepped forth.
1.4.2.9 Here he places fuel-sticks upon the fire.
1.4.2.10 He gives a pair [of animals] at the *samits*; he offers an oblation for the *daśahotṛ* with four ladlings into the *gārhapatya* fire, which is capable of bearing the oblations.
1.4.2.11 With the verse "We cry out to thee, O hero" (*abhi tvā śūra nonuma*), he worships with the *rathantara* [sāman].
1.4.2.12 He binds a faggot of one hundred stalks of *darbha* grass.

1.4.2.13 They kindle the sacrificial fuel (idhma), they prepare the supporting ladles (upayamanī), and they bring forward an ox that has been washed. 1.4.2.14 They wait for the rising sun with the Āhavanīya fire.
1.4.2.15 Once the sun has risen, he lifts up the sacrificial fuel with three verses beginning: "For vigor and strength, I lift thee up."
1.4.2.16. With the verse, "Go forth toward the eastern quarter, O wise one," they set out with the ox-drawn cart first.
1.4.2.17. They arrive at the *viṣuvat* (the central day). Standing there, he says, "Pour down the ritual materials for the *anvāhāryapacana* fire.
1.4.2.18. With the formula, "I spread the *ṛta*, the soil upon the earth," he pours down half of the ritual materials once the site for the *anvāhāryapacana* fire has been excavated.
1.4.2.19 He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "From the Real I place truth; upon truth, Mātariśvan, Vāyu, and Agni I place.
1.4.2.20 He says, "Pour out the fire"; he consecrates it with the mantra, "The earth by its abundance...
1.4.2.21 Seated to the south, while the Adhvaryu sits to the north, he throws down a piece of gold weighing eight *pṛḍa*s with the words, "O Ordainer, bestow prosperity upon me."

1.4.2.22 He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Make me the overlord for prosperity; may Indra, the bountiful lord of the quarters, anoint me with glory. I leave behind exhaustion, lack of food, and disease; unite with my dear body.
1.4.2.23 At the midpoint (viṣuvat), he worships a piece of gold placed there with the verse: "May these riches attend upon me," and [he approaches] the unscattered *pṛdāku* snake.
1.4.2.24 With the verse, "In what way has the wonderful one appeared to us?", they proceed beyond the midpoint with the Vāmadevya chant.

1.4.2.25 He causes the ox to step forward toward the east with its right foot upon the northern side of the offering-ground. 1.4.2.26 Again, turning back toward the west, he does so with that same [foot]. 1.4.2.27 He releases it toward the north.
1.4.2.28 He pours down the ritual materials with the offering [of earth] while reciting: "I spread the *ṛta* as soil upon the earth.
1.4.2.29 He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Upon the *ṛta* I establish the *satya*; upon the *satya* I establish Mātariśvan, Sūrya, and Agni"; thus he completes the *yajus*.
1.4.2.30 He pours down the supporting earth (*upayamani*).

1.4.2.31 He settles [the fire] with all five [verses], beginning with "O Agni, you are light, you are the world, you are the earth," for the Āhavanīya fire. 1.4.2.32 With the formula, "By the vow of those gods, O Lord of Vows, I settle thee," he settles it according to whichever deity [the sacrificer] belongs to. With "By the Gāyatrī metre," [he settles it] for a Brāhmaṇa; with "By the Triṣṭubh metre," for a Rājanya; with "By the Jagatī metre," for a Vaiśya.
1.4.2.33 While seated to the south, the Adhvaryu, [reciting] "Bestow upon me prosperity, bestow wealth," throws down eight pieces of gold to the north of him.

1.4.2.34 He causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Make me the overlord for prosperity; may Indra Maghavan, the lord of the quarters, anoint me with glory; I abandon exhaustion, lack of nourishment, and disease; unite with my dear body.
1.4.2.35 With the verse beginning "That which here from heaven," he worships the *sanna* (the settled oblation).
1.4.2.36 The rite succeeds up to the preparation of the oblation (*haviṣkḷpti*).

1.4.2.37–39. From this point on, it is the preparation of the oblation. Having set out the sacrificial implements and having carried forward the waters, he offers a cake on eight potsherds for Agni. This sacrificial cake is "within the body. When it has been cooked and placed [on the altar], he touches it with this *yajus*: "O Agni, that body of yours which is purifying (*pavamānā*), with that I endow you; O Agni, that body of yours which is purifying (*pāvakā*), with that I endow you; O Agni, that body of yours which is bright (*śuci*), with that I endow you. Thus, it becomes entirely dedicated to Agni.
1.4.2.40 Regarding his *sāmidhenī* verses, he omits the verse beginning with "pra vo vājā," for this one is undefined.
1.4.2.41 Here he inserts the verse beginning with "vājayann iva nū rathān" and [the verse] beginning with "yogām agner upastuhi yaśastamasya mīḍhuṣaḥ.
1.4.2.42 He omits the verse beginning with "tan tvā samidbhir aṅgira," for this one is undefined.
1.4.2.43. At this point, he places this verse: "O best of the Aṅgiras, O Agni, most skilled disposer, may we speak to you a dear and winning prayer.
1.4.2.E. The ritual proceeds successfully up to the *prayāja* offerings.
1.4.3.1 The ritual action is established up until the *prayāja* offerings.
1.4.3.2 Having uttered the case endings, he pronounces the *vaṣaṭ* for the *prayāja* offerings.

1.4.3.3 He says, "O, cause [them] to hear! and then, "Sacrifice to the *samidhs*. 1.4.3.4 He pronounces the case-ending: "We who sacrifice to Agni," and for the *samidhs*, "O Agni, may the *samidhs* partake of the clarified butter (*ājya*). He utters the *vaṣaṭ* call.
1.4.3.5 He follows with the recitation: "Come for the feast; being praised for the giving of the oblation, sit down as the Hotṛ-priest upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*)."

1.4.3.6 He says, "Make [the sacrificer] hear! and "Recite the offering prayer! (yaja). 1.4.3.7 He pronounces the case-ending: "We who sacrifice to Agni," and he utters the *vaṣaṭ* call: "May Tanūnapāt, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter.
1.4.3.8 He follows with the consecratory formula: "We choose the messenger, the all-knowing Hotṛ of this sacrifice, the one of good wisdom."
1.4.3.9 He says, "O, cause [the Hotṛ] to hear! and "Recite the offering prayer (yaja)!
1.4.3.10 He pronounces the case-ending: "Those whom we worship with Agni... and performs the *vaṣaṭ* call with the words, "...may the *iḍas* of the clarified butter partake, O Agni!
1.4.3.11 He follows the rite with the mantra: "Agni is being kindled... the sage, the master of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, whose mouth is the sacrificial ladle."

1.4.3.12 He says, "Make [the gods] hear! and "Sacrifice! 1.4.3.13 He pronounces the case-ending: "We who sacrifice to Agni," and "May the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) enjoy the clarified butter (*ājya*), O Agni! and he utters the *vaṣaṭ* call.
1.4.3.14 He follows with the consecration formula: "May he strike down the Vṛtras," and "Desiring wealth, through inspired praise, the kindled, bright one, well-invoked."
1.4.3.15 The final fore-offering (prayāja) is performed spontaneously.
1.4.3.16 He performs the two butter-portions (ājyabhāga), [reciting] the two butter-portions for Budhanvat.
1.4.3.17 Saying "Recite for Agni," while taking up the clarified butter four times, he recites [the verse] beginning with "Awake, O Agni."
1.4.3.18 He sacrifices with [the verse] beginning *juṣāṇa*; he offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.

1.4.3.19 [The Adhvaryu] says, "Recite for Agni Pavamāna," while taking a portion of clarified butter (*ājya*). [The Hotṛ] recites four verses beginning, "Agni is the seer," followed by, "Pavamāna, the priest of the five peoples, him we seek, the possessor of great wealth.
1.4.3.20 [He continues] with, "Come hither, O Soma, I shall speak to thee," and, lying near [the butter], with, "O Agni, these other songs [are for thee]; mayest thou grow strong by these drops."
1.4.3.21 He sacrifices with [the verse] beginning "juṣāṇa" (enjoying) and offers at the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ* call.
1.4.3.22 Saying "Recite for Agni," he speaks while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portion].
1.4.3.23 The *yājyā* and *anuvākyā* verses consist of *paṅkti* meters.
1.4.3.24 He recites, "O Agni, him today... (RV 8.44.1).
1.4.3.25 He performs the sacrifice with, "For thus, O Agni... (RV 8.44.27), and offers the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.
1.4.3.26 With, "Return with strength... (RV 8.44.16), he offers a spoonful (*sruvāhuti*) before the cake-offering; with, "Return with wealth... (RV 8.44.16), he offers one after it.
1.4.3.27. He says, "Recite for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt," while spreading [the butter] and cutting [the portions].

1.4.3.28. He recites [the invitatory verse], "With these songs today for thee... 1.4.3.29. He offers the oblation with [the offering verse], "With these our hymns..."; when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he pours the offering.
1.4.3.30 Having stepped across and placed the two offering-spoons in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion.
1.4.3.31 Having touched water, he cuts off the *iḍā* portion.
1.4.3.32 When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places it for the *agnīdh*.

1.4.3.33 They consume [the portions] and perform the ritual purification; they carry [the fire] around. 1.4.3.34 When the *prāśitra* has been consumed by the *brahmán*, the *āgnīdh* sits down at the rubbish heap (*utkara*) with a water-pot.
1.4.3.35 At this point, he gives as the fee for the re-establishment of the fires (*punarādheya*) a chariot repaired again, a garment sewn again, and an ox released again.
1.4.3.36 He offers the oblation following the continuity of the Hotṛ’s [recitation]. 1.4.3.E The ritual proceeds successfully up to the after-offerings (anūyāja).
1.4.4.1 The ritual action is completed up to the *anūyāja* offerings.
1.4.4.2 Having uttered the case-endings for the two *anūyāja* offerings, he pronounces the *vaṣaṭ* call.
1.4.4.3 He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! and "Sacrifice to the gods! (devān yaja).
1.4.4.4 He pronounces the case-ending: "of Agni. He utters the *vaṣaṭ* call: "May the divine sacrificial grass enjoy the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth!
1.4.4.5 He follows with the consecration formula: "We meditate upon the hymn—may it be successful today, touching the sky, for the sake of the god Draviṇasvat.
1.4.4.6 He says, "O, cause [the offering] to be heard! and "Sacrifice! (yaja).
1.4.4.7 He recites the case-ending: "We who sacrifice to Agni"; he pronounces the *vaṣaṭ* call with: "May the divine Narāśaṃsa partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth.
1.4.4.8 He follows with the consecratory formula: "The mortal who [offers] service... and "...may he, enjoying the prayer with prayers, be the first to enjoy the many dawns.
1.4.4.9 The final after-offering (*anūyāja*) is spontaneously accomplished.
1.4.4.10 The ritual action is successfully accomplished up to the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings.

1.4.4.11 One should employ verses for the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings that are characterized by the word "Agni"; having merely uttered "O Agni," one should recite the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) or perform the offering verse (*yājyā*). 1.4.4.12 The ritual action is successfully accomplished; this sacrifice is concluded.

1.4.4.13 Having arranged the sacrificial implements and having led forward the waters, he offers a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra and Agni, and a pap to Āditya. 1.4.4.14 This sacrifice is thus prepared.
1.4.4.15 This indeed is the "double-grass" rite for prosperity and the re-establishment of the fires.
1.4.4.16 Now, regarding the re-establishment of the fires that were previously extinguished: these same materials for the two sets [of fires] are used, with the exception of the two bundles of grass.
1.4.4.17 At the proper time, he places the fuel-sticks on the fire.
1.4.4.18 The ritual procedure is completed up to the verses addressed to the Queen of Serpents.

1.4.4.19 Having worshipped with the *sarparājñī* verses, he worships with the three subsequent verses: "May the mind, the light, enjoy that which thou, when angry, didst scatter away; that which was scattered by thy wrath.
1.4.4.20 The ritual procedure is established up to the *agnihotra*.
1.4.4.21 He offers the *agnihotra* with the verse: "Seven, O Agni, are thy fuel-sticks; seven are thy tongues."
1.4.4.22 The rite is successfully accomplished for the sake of continuity with the first offering.

1.4.4.23 Following the continuity, he offers three spoonfuls (sruva) with [the formulas]: "Lekas, Salekas, Sulekas; Ketas, Saketas, Suketas; Vivasvān, Aditi, Devajūti. 1.4.4.24 The rite is successfully accomplished; this sacrifice is concluded.
1.4.4.25 Having arranged the sacrificial implements and having led forward the waters, he offers a cake on eleven potsherds to Agni and Varuṇa as an after-offering.
1.4.4.26 For this [offering], there are two butter-portions rich in wealth, and for the oblation, [the verses] are according to the respective deities.
1.4.4.27 The two Virāj verses are the concluding offering-verses (*saṃyājye*).
1.4.4.28 He offers the oblation following the continuity of the Hotṛ’s [recitation]. 1.4.4.29 The rite is successfully accomplished; this sacrifice is concluded.
1.4.4.30 Having arranged the sacrificial implements and having carried forward the waters, he offers an oblation on eleven potsherds for Indra and Agni, and a pap for Āditya.

1.4.4.31 This very sacrifice is thus prepared. 1.4.4.32 This is called *tribarhis*, [and it is] for one who has piled [the fire-altar] and then re-established it. 1.4.4.33 But he should not go even in the direction of his own shadow. Wherever he might perceive this rite being performed, from there he should go toward another direction for the whole day, until the setting of the sun.
End of the *Punarādheya* section of the *Vādhūla Śrautasūtra* 1.5–1.6 [Agnihotra, Agnyupasthāna]. Manuscripts:
K1, K2, K3, N1, N2, M, C, T1, T2 (as variant readings of T1).
1.5.1.1 Intending to attend upon the fires that have been drawn out, he enters between the Gārhapatya and the Anvāhāryapacana fires and sits down to the south of the Āhavanīya fire.
1.5.1.2 Now, when he is about to offer the *agnihotra*, he carries water around [the fire].
1.5.1.3 He touches that [water] with the formula: "Thou art lightning; light up my evil.
1.5.1.4 Then, with the formula: "O waters, sustainers of the vow, place the vow in me; place faith in me," he sips water.
1.5.1.5 He summons the Agnihotrī cow with: "O *Iḍā*, come! Rest in me! O *Iḍā*, come! Rest in me! O *Śraddhā*, come! I summon you by means of truth.
1.5.1.6 Pointing to the altar (*vedi*), he should say: "You are this [earth]. Of you, Agni is the calf. Through that calf, O Agni, milk for me faith, austerity, and that desire.
1.5.1.7 Whatever desire he desires, that he invokes. Truly, that desire is fulfilled for him.

1.5.1.8 Restraining his speech, having gone around the front of the Āhavanīya fire, he draws out embers from the Gārhapatya fire towards the north with the formula: "You are the makers of beings. 1.5.1.9 Having made them separate, he takes [the milk] with the formula: "O Agni, I take the Āditya; from night, I take the day. 1.5.1.10 With the formula:
"O well-being, settle yourself," he places it over the fire.
1.5.1.11 With the words, "Rising, the heavenly world," he illumines [it]; with the words, "Shine forth in the three worlds," he causes it to shine.

1.5.1.12 With the words, "O waters, you are rising," he pours water back with the *sruva* spoon, saying, "Make this sacrificer rise up with offspring and cattle. 1.5.1.13 With the words, "Rising, the heavenly world," he thus illumines [it]; with the words, "Shine forth in the three worlds," he causes it to shine.
1.5.1.14 With the words, "The *rakṣas* is excluded, the enemies are excluded," he performs the circumambulation with fire three times while moving forward.

1.5.1.15 Having cut off [the grass], he throws away the illuminator with the words, "Struck away is failure, struck away is the evil of bad dreams, struck away is evil, struck away is the evil of the evildoer; may the evil deed that another does to us return upon him.
1.5.1.16 Having thrown the illuminator into the fire, he extinguishes it.

1.5.1.17 Having set down the ashes three times with [the formulas], "Thou art Viṣṇu’s stride; thou art Viṣṇu’s step; thou art Viṣṇu’s wide stride," he establishes [the fire] with the fourth [formula]. 1.5.1.18 Having caused himself and the embers to tremble, he pushes them away toward the outside with [the formula], "He has made it well-being. 1.5.1.E Having made them well-pushed-away, he takes up the dipping-spoon (*sruva*) and a fuel-stick (*samidh*) with his right hand.
1.5.2.1 With his right hand he takes the *sruva* ladle and the fuel-sticks, and with his left hand the *sruc* ladle.
1.5.2.2 He heats them over the *gārhapatya* fire [with the mantra]: "The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away."
1.5.2.3 Having heated [the ladle], he says: "I draw up.
1.5.2.4 "Draw up for the gods the oblation, for me, for fearlessness!

1.5.2.5 He draws it up: with "May *iḍā* be," he draws the first ladling; with "May *iḍā* generate," the second; with "May *iḍā* increase," the third; with "May *iḍā* act," the fourth; and with "Heavenly *iḍā*," the fifth, if there are five ladlings.
1.5.2.6 Having drawn [the portion], he touches it with: "In harmony with the gods who travel in the evening. 1.5.2.7 When it has been drawn, he recites the Daśahotṛ formula.
1.5.2.8 Having stood up, he carries [the vessel] at the height of his mouth, saying: "Propitiate Agni Vaiśvānara."
1.5.2.9 At the Viṣuvat [sacrifice], he lifts [the spoon].

1.5.2.10 Having placed the *sruk* on the grass-bundle (*kūrca*), he places a fuel-stick upon it with the formula: "I place thee, the silver-colored, lighted by fire, accompanied by Vāyu, leading to heaven, as an imperishable brick for the heavenly world—for the sake of the night. I place immortality in the breath. May Prajāpati settle thee on the back of the earth. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras!
1.5.2.11 Then, over a portion of this size, he offers the fuel-sticks with the mantra: "Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā!"

1.5.2.12 Having offered [the oblation], he breathes over it [with the formula]: "I place the immortal breath within me; may the breath enter me together with immortality, for the sake of peace and freedom from burning.
1.5.2.13 Then he looks at this oblation. 1.5.2.14 That which is offered in the *gārhapatya* fire, he offers mentally [with the formula]: "To Agni Gṛhapati, svāhā!"

1.5.2.15 Having followed the oblation of the *hotṛ* with the recitation, he offers the second oblation to the north. 1.5.2.16 Having offered it, he breathes in [the vapā] with the formula: "I place immortality in my out-breath; may the out-breath enter me together with immortality, for the sake of peace and to prevent burning.
1.5.2.17 Having pushed [the vapā] forward and placed the ladle on the grass-bunch, he wipes the ladle towards the west.
1.5.2.18 He wipes his hand forward on the *kūrca* grass mat.
1.5.2.19 Having wiped it a second time toward the north, he wipes it a second time outside the altar to the south.
1.5.2.20 He consumes [the food] twice without making the sound *cuk*.

1.5.2.21 Right there, having turned toward the north, he consumes [the remnant] with the formula: "The Agni-light, bright, generative, rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in wealth, rich in prosperity, rich in fields; of thee, who art drunk by Agni, full of sweetness, and invited, I, being invited, consume.
1.5.2.22 Rising, he makes a dedication.
1.5.2.23 Having sipped water twice and rinsed his mouth twice, he pours out the contents of the offering-ladle.

1.5.2.24 Having thoroughly cleansed the *sruk* ladle and handed it over, he proceeds while restraining his speech; having circumambulated the *āhavanīya* fire from the front, he gazes at the fires, saying: "Fearlessness for you, fearlessness for me, fearlessness for me, fearlessness for you. [He gazes] at the *āhavanīya* with "Thou art life," at the *gārhapatya* with "Thou art the life of all," at the *anvāhāryapacana* with "Thou art the fullness of life," and again at the *āhavanīya* with "Thou art the thread. Then [he says]: "From that thou art, from that I am thine, from that thou art mine; extend thyself along with me."

"May I, so-and-so, be rich in offspring and cattle," with these words he first pronounces his own name; then, in succession, "May so-and-so be rich [in offspring and cattle], may so-and-so be rich [in offspring and cattle]," and finally at the end, "May my lineage flourish.
"O Agni, you who are full of light...
1.5.3.1 With the words, "O Agni, full of light, may I, full of light, kindle thee," he kindles the Āhavanīya fire. With the words, "For the mind, for the heavenly world, thee," he worships it.
1.5.3.2 With the words, "O Agni, full of life, may I, full of life, kindle thee," he kindles the Gārhapatya fire. [With the words,] "For life, thee... that desire is fulfilled.
1.5.3.E Whatever is thine, O Suśīmā...

1.5.4.1 With the words, “O Suśīmā, that heart of yours which is within the beginning and the end in Prajāpati—you know that nectar; may I not weep for the sin of my grandson,” he touches her. [He thinks: “I know the hidden heart of Suśīmā within Prajāpati.”

1.5.4.2 "Know me for him; may I not weep over the sin of my grandson, may I not wail over the sin of my grandson"—having worshipped the fires with this [verse], he goes out in this very manner and stands by the *gārhapatya* fire: "O Agni, protect us! O Indra, save us! O Soma, be gracious! O Aditi, guard us! O Vaiśvānara, you are light; protect me! You are the light of Mitra and Varuṇa; protect me! May those who pierce from afar find us not; may those who pierce from close range find us not. Let the arrows and the shafts of Indra be turned away from us!"

"Cast down [the arrows] in all directions; let the missiles fly away from us—those that have been shot and those yet to be shot, whether divine or human. Pierce our rivals! O gods, let them harm whoever is our rival, whoever is not our rival, and whoever acts with hostility. May the sacred word (*brahman*) be my inner armor.
(1.5.4.3) Having performed the worship with the *brahmavarman* formula, he may lie down at his pleasure—at night, according to this rule.
(1.5.4.4) Then, in the morning, when the ritual has been successfully completed, [he rises] from the removal of the embers.
1.5.4.5 Having made [the cups] empty, he draws [the cup] with the formula: "I draw Agni for Āditya; day for night. 1.5.4.6 The ritual action is completed by the touching [of the cup].
1.5.4.7 Having drawn it up, he touches it with the formula: "In harmony with the gods who travel at dawn."
1.5.4.8 The ritual action is perfected by the placing of the fuel-sticks (*samidh*).

1.5.4.9 He places a fuel-stick with the formula: “Thee, the golden-hued, whose light is the sun, possessed of wind, leading to heaven—for the sake of the heavenly world—I place as an imperishable brick, day by day. I place immortality in the breath. May Prajāpati settle thee on the back of the sky. By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit thou firm. 1.5.4.10 Then he offers these two fuel-sticks with the formula: “Sūrya is the light, light is Sūrya, svāhā!”
1.5.4.11 The ritual action becomes perfected through wiping.
1.5.4.12 He wipes the *sruva* ladle toward the east.
1.5.4.13 He wipes his hand, turned westward, on the *kūrca* grass-mat.
1.5.4.14 Having wiped it a second time on the north side, he wipes it a second time outside the altar toward the south.
1.5.4.15 He consumes [the remnant] twice without making the sound "cuk".

1.5.4.16 Turning back toward the north right there, he consumes it with the formula: "The light of Sūrya, bright, generative, rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in wealth, rich in offspring, rich in fields; of thee, who art drunk by Sūrya, full of sweetness, invited, I consume thee, being invited."
1.5.4.17 The ritual action is accomplished. 1.5.4.18 Without attending to the fires, he gazes at them [saying]: "Homage be to you; may my faith not depart.
[End of Agnihotra]
1.6 The Worship of the Fires (Agnī-upasthāna).
1.6.1.1 He is about to worship the fires; for him, a cow that has calved for the first time and has a male calf is prepared as the *agnihotrī*.
1.6.1.2 If she has neither a male nor a female calf, [it is] as if she had a female calf.

1.6.1.3 If he establishes the fires under a lunar mansion, he begins with that which is his "approach" (upaniśānta) rite for attending the fires, continuing until the full-moon or new-moon festival. 1.6.1.4 But if he establishes the fires on a festival day, he begins with this very same [rite].
1.6.1.5 Having caused [the calf] to suckle, they tie this calf [to the sacrificial post].

1.6.1.6 Having placed the sacred thread over the left shoulder and having sipped water, standing in the sacrificer’s station, he pays homage to the Āhavanīya fire. 1.6.1.7 “He should pay homage as if slightly obliquely,” so says the Brāhmaṇa. He pays homage as if slightly obliquely with the verses according to their meters, beginning with “Going forward to the sacrifice,” and ending with “O Citrāvasu, may I reach your safe shore. From there...
1.6.1.8 He meditates upon the night with his mind, saying: "O thou of variegated wealth, may I reach thy end in safety.

1.6.1.9 He places a fuel-stick on the fire with the verse: "Kindling thee for a hundred winters," and [continues]: "Radiant, we kindle thee; full of vigor, upon the highest firmament, svāhā! 1.6.1.10 With this same verse, he should place three [fuel-sticks] in succession.

1.6.1.11 Now, regarding the single [brick]: one should place this very same brick three times. For there is indeed a Brāhmaṇa passage: "This is indeed the *sūrmī* (metal image) with ears; by means of it, the gods used to strike down the Asuras a hundredfold, so that their efforts were not in vain.

1.6.1.12 This is the Brāhmaṇa for the single [brick]: "One should place one," and thus he places only one; this is the established rule. 1.6.1.13 He worships [the fire] with the verse: "O Agni, may you be united with the splendor of Sūrya; be united with the praise of the seers, and with offspring. Thus he concludes.
1.6.1.14 He says, "May they fashion themselves for you, O sacrificer; meditate upon that which is elsewhere in your mind.

1.6.1.15 He consecrates that which has been fashioned with the mantra: "I behold the offspring; may they be many for me. 1.6.1.16 With the words, "You are united, possessing all forms," he touches the calf of the Agnihotra cow while standing facing eastward to the north of the Anvāhāryapacana fire, as if toward its right eye-socket: "Come to me with vigor, with lordship over cattle, and with abundance of wealth; let them resort to wealth."

1.6.1.17 Then, having gone westward, he worships the Gārhapatya fire with six verses: "Up to thee, O Agni, day by day... ruling over the sacrifices... as a father to his son... O Agni, thou art our closest [friend]... that thee, O most radiant one, shining one... Agni is the Vasu, renowned for wealth.

1.6.1.18 With the words, "With vigor I look upon you; look upon me with vigor," he gazes at the houses. With the words, "With abundance of wealth I look upon you; look upon me with abundance of wealth," he gazes at the cows.

1.6.1.19 With the words, "Ye are the *iḍās*, honey-makers," he [addresses] those very [cows]; with the words, "Be gracious to me; enter me for the sake of wealth," 1.6.1.20 then, having gone forward to the east, he worships the Āhavanīya fire with four verses: "That excellent splendor of Savitṛ," "The exhilarating Soma," "Never art thou barren," and "O Agni, we [take] thee as a fortress.

1.6.1.21 Then, having gone back to the west, he worships the Gārhapatya fire with the verse: "O Agni, Lord of the House, may I be a good lord of the house through thee as lord of the house; mayst thou be a good lord of the house through me as lord of the house."

1.6.1.22 He pronounces the blessings: “A hundred winters—this blessing I pronounce for myself and for so-and-so, full of light. First he mentions his own name, then those of [the others] in order, saying “for so-and-so, for so-and-so,” ending finally with “for the sons, the lineages.

1.6.1.23 This is its Brāhmaṇa: “He who worships the Āhavanīya falls away from this world; he worships the Gārhapatya and thus finds firm support in this very world; moreover, he makes amends to the Gārhapatya. This is that which has been stated.
1.6.1.E Now, one [rite] is common up to the sixth [day].
1.6.2.1 Now, one [verse] is the same up to the sixth [verse].
1.6.2.2 With six [verses], he worships the Gārhapatya fire.

1.6.2.3 He gazes at the houses [with the words]: “I gaze upon you for strength; gaze upon me with strength. 1.6.2.4 Having gone forward to the east, he worships the Āhavanīya fire with three verses: “That excellent splendor of Savitṛ... [the verse] beginning with *somānaṃ svaraṇam*... [and the verse] beginning with *kadā cana starīr asi*.
1.6.2.5 The verse beginning with “*pari tvāgne puram vayam*” remains as a concluding prayer (*pariśeṣa*).
1.6.2.6 Then, having gone back toward the west, he worships the Gārhapatya fire with [the verse], "O Agni, lord of the house... (VS 3.29).
1.6.2.7 In this very same manner, he invokes blessings.
1.6.2.8 Having gone forward to the east, he worships the Āhavanīya fire with [the verse], "Around thee, O Agni, as a fortress... (VS 3.27).
1.6.2.9 Regarding this, the Brāhmaṇa says: "O Agni, we [place] a fortress around you"—he says this; he thus places this very enclosure around [the fire] so that nothing may spill over.
1.6.2.10 Now, one [verse] is common up to the sixth [offering].

1.6.2.11 Having worshipped the Gārhapatya fire with six verses, he worships from that very spot [the Āhavanīya] with the verse: "O Agni, lord of the house... (RV 7.1.14). 1.6.2.12 In the same manner, he invokes blessings.

1.6.2.13 Having gone forward to the east, he worships the Āhavanīya fire with four verses: "That excellent glory of Savitṛ... (RV 3.62.10), "Soma, the one who makes us hear... (RV 1.91.1), "Never art thou barren... (RV 8.51.7), and "Around thee, O Agni, we build a fortress... (RV 10.8.6).

1.6.2.14 This [rite] is performed facing eastward; one thereby attains this Brāhmaṇa passage: "O Agni, we [take refuge] in thee as in a fortress"—this is the first [verse], and "O dwelling" is the second.

1.6.2.15 With this very [formula], he worships at evening alone, not in the morning; he worships at night. 1.6.2.16 For the Brāhmaṇa says, "Not in the morning. On the following day, he recites the Āgnipāvamānī verses; these are the six ṛcs beginning with "O Agni, thou purifiest our lives."
1.6.2.17 One does not perform the *upasthāna* (reverential salutation) for a year with the *agnipāvamānī* verses.

1.6.2.18 “After the year has passed, one performs the *upasthāna* with the *agnipāvamānī* verses. Therefore, from this point onward, he may perform the *upasthāna* with the *agnipāvamānī* verses at his pleasure; he may also remove [the fire] at his pleasure. 1.6.2.19 Regarding this, there is this *brāhmaṇa*: “Just as a man, a horse, or a cow grows old, even so does the fire grow old; yet it also purifies. This is that which is stated.

1.6.2.20 This very worship of the fire (*agnyupasthāna*) bestows long life, secures the world, procures sons, and brings cattle. Indeed, he who worships with this becomes long-lived, a possessor of the world, a father of sons, and rich in cattle. In this very worship of the fire, all meters, all blessings, and all desires are contained. 1.6.2.21 Verily, for him who worships with this, there is no meter left unfulfilled, no blessing omitted, and no desire unattained.

1.6.2.22 Just as this great sacrifice is performed with all the meters, even so is his *agnihotra* performed with all the meters by him who worships it with this [rite]. 1.6.2.23 Now, the *Māhācamasa*:
"O Agni, you who are full of light..."
"O Agni, full of light, may I, full of light, kindle thee," with these words he kindles the Āhavanīya fire. "For the mind, for the heavenly world, [I kindle] thee.
Indeed, that desire of his which he approaches with this [rite] is fulfilled.
1.6.3.E Now, the ritual for returning from a journey.
1.6.4.1 Now, the ritual for returning from a journey.
1.6.4.2 When departing on a journey, he protects the time for the removal of the fires by fasting, and the *agnihotra* by restraining his speech.

1.6.4.3 When he thinks that the oblation has been offered, he puts on the sacrificial cord (*yajñopavīta*), sips water, and—standing facing east or north, or sitting—he mutters: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ! O Agnis, being about to be invoked; O Agnis, being invoked; O Agnis, having been invoked: protect my well-offered and well-poured oblation! Protect me by means of *ṛta* and *satya*; protect me by day and night; protect me by out-breath and in-breath! May I prosper with two-footed beings; may I prosper with four-footed beings! May I attain the day; may I attain the night"—thus at evening. "May I attain the night; may I attain the day"—thus in the morning. For the day is *ṛta*, and the night is *satya*.
1.6.4.4 Moreover, indeed, for him who worships with this [rite], even what has not been offered becomes as if offered.
