1.6.4.5 Now follows the worship performed out of sight: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ! Being right here, O Agnis, for you who are there, I sustain you with breath, speech, and mind. May life not abandon me while I am hidden; I worship you with the Vaiśvānara light.
1.6.4.6 Then, having returned, he worships with the *māhāsāmpada* formula: "Om" to the Gārhapatya fire; "Om" to the Anvāhāryapacana fire; "Om" to the Āhavanīya fire.

1.6.4.7 With "Oṃ," indeed, is one praised; with "Oṃ," is one recited; with "Oṃ," is the *āśrāvaṇa* call made. 1.6.4.8 Now, for him who worships in this manner, each [deity] becomes attended by the three Vedas three times over.
1.6.4.9 Then, in the established manner, he silently places the third set of fuel-sticks (*samidh*) upon the fire.

1.6.4.10 Now follows the enkindling [of the fire]: with the verse, "This is your womb, according to the season," he causes the fire to ascend into the two kindling woods; with the verse, "From which you were born... [grant us] wealth. 1.6.4.11 Now, moreover, they say: "If [the fire] that has ascended into the two kindling woods should be lost, his fire would perish; there would be a need for a re-establishment [of the sacred fires]."

1.6.4.12 “O Agni, with that body of yours which is worthy of sacrifice, come here; ascend!”—reciting thus, while mentally depositing [the fire] within himself, he should exhale three times: “Making the self for the self, bringing many riches to us, O manly one; having become the sacrifice, sit upon the sacrifice, O Jātavedas, in your own womb; being born, come to your dwelling. 1.6.4.13 Then follows the descent: “Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ! O you of beautiful countenance, being invoked; all the gods and the sacrificer, sit down!”

1.6.4.14 Then the second [verse]: "Descend again, O Jātavedas; knowing our way, carry the oblation to the gods for us. Bestow upon us long life, progeny, and wealth; shine forever within our dwellings.
1.6.4.15 [One may perform this] with both [verses] or with one.
1.6.4.16 Now, therefore, follows the expiation for fires that have gone out.

1.6.4.17 If all [the fires] should go out, having consigned them to their respective hearths with the formula, "This is your seasonal womb," having lifted them up, having sprinkled this ash, having churned [the fire], and having distributed the fires, he offers the *santati* oblation; then he performs the established *agnihotra*.

1.6.4.18 Then, for the second time, having consigned them to their respective hearths with the very same formula, "This is your seasonal womb," having lifted them up, having sprinkled this ash, having churned [the fire], and having distributed the fires, he offers the *santati* oblation together with the *vyāhṛtis*; then he performs the established *agnihotra*.

1.6.4.19 Now, for the third [kind of sacrifice], having caused [the fires] to ascend by means of the verse, "This is your seasonal womb," he removes the hearths, scatters this very ash, sprinkles water, churns [the fire], and having spread out the fires, he proceeds with the Hotṛ priests in the established manner, ending with the full-oblation (pūrṇāhuti).
1.6.4.20 Then he performs the Agnihotra in its established form.

1.6.4.21 Now, for the fourth [offering]: having caused the fires to ascend by means of the formula, "This is thy seasonal womb," and having likewise lifted them up, having sprinkled the ashes, and having churned [the fire], he worships the Gārhapatya with eight verses: "May all the gods lift thee up; awaken, O Agni! Lead him upward to higher realms; may we rise up out of the darkness. O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us. May the mind, as light, enjoy [the oblation]. Spinning the thread, thou, O Agni, art far-extending, the beloved and excellent Hotṛ."

Having worshipped with these verses, "By you [the sacrifice] is spread... and so forth, he offers four oblations of four-draughts each, or he stands near [the fire] with the verses: "O Agni Aṅgiras," "O Agni Abhyāvartin," "With strength again," and "Together with wealth.
Then he draws it out [from the Gārhapatya] with: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ; by means of speech, thee, for the office of the Hotṛ."

1.6.5.1 "With speech as the *hotṛ*, with breath as the *udgātṛ*, with the eye as the *adhvaryu*, with the mind as the *brahman*, and with the ear as the *agnīdh*—with these five divine officiating priests (*ṛtvij*), I lift you up. As you are being lifted up, lift me up from evil: whatever I have done unknowingly and whatever I have done knowingly, whatever sin has been committed by day—being lifted up, release me from all that. Thus [he says] at evening. "Whatever sin has been committed by night—being lifted up, release me from all that."

Therefore, at dawn, unite with the beloved body of the Sun and Agni! O invincible one, fierce one, conqueror of armies, unassailable one! Be a pleasant womb; the earth is a pleasant womb. May he who seeks to cross over you not overcome you! You are vigor, you are force, you are strength, you are brilliance, you are glory, you are fortune, you are the slayer of Vṛtra. Whoever assails us—whether he be of our own kin or a stranger—him, O Agni, do you slay with that [weapon]! With the mountain of sacred power (*brahman*), I press down upon my hateful rival, an offering of immortality for the immortal; I offer Agni into the immortal.

"On the earth, for the winning of immortality; by that may I win that infinite desire which Prajāpati won first: *agnim agnau svāhā*—thus at evening; *sūryam agnau svāhā*—thus in the morning. (1.6.5.2) Then he offers the established Agnihotra. (1.6.5.3) Now follows the Kauṣītaka: "*bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ, vāk āyuḥ, vāk ca vāyuś ca, viśvāyuḥ, viśvam āyuḥ, sarvāyuḥ, sarvam āyuḥ*. (1.6.5.4)
1.6.5.4 He who worships with this indeed attains a full lifespan.

1.6.5.5 Now, [the formulas] for the fifth [offering]: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ! To you, the god Agni, I offer the secret names, forms, and beings. May my intention be fulfilled; may the Lord of Mind fulfill it for me; may faith not depart from me"—this is at evening. "To you, the god Sūrya..."—this is in the morning.

1.6.5.6 This much indeed exists: namely, these auspicious secret names, forms, and beings. Verily, *ākūti* (intention) becomes successful for him whose lord of the mind is [thus established]; his faith does not depart from him who worships with this. 1.6.5.7 Now follows the Paiṅga: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! May I be rich in good offspring through my offspring, rich in brave sons through my sons, rich in splendor through my splendor, and rich in nourishment through my nourishments.

1.6.5.8 Verily, he who worships with this becomes rich in good offspring through his offspring, rich in brave sons through his sons, rich in splendor through his splendor, and rich in nourishment through his nourishments.
1.6.5.9 Or else, with the *vārkala* formula: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Homage be to you! Let there be fearlessness for you! Let there be fearlessness for me! O Great One!
1.6.5.10 Indeed, fearlessness and greatness come to him who worships with this.
1.6.5.11 Now, the worship of the Vaiśya is: "May it be auspicious for you! May it be very auspicious for you! May there be auspiciousness and greater wealth for me!"

1.6.5.12 He indeed becomes more prosperous and better off for whomsoever he worships with this [rite]. 1.6.5.13 Then, as they were originally established, he worships: with "Bhūḥ" the Gārhapatya fire; with "Bhuvaḥ" the Anvāhāryapacana fire; with "Suvaḥ" the Āhavanīya fire; and with "The essence of the Vedas.
1.6.5.14 Then, with one [verse]: "May I be able to support [thee]."
1.6.5.15 Then one [should recite]: "May my faith not fail.

1.6.5.16 Then one [should recite]: "For whatever desire Prajāpati offered the Agnihotra, may I fulfill that desire; may that be the blessing of the Agnihotra, may that blessing be mine. With these two oblations, by means of the Gāyatrī metre, the Trivṛt stoma, the Rathantara Sāman, the Vaṣaṭ-call, and the thunderbolt, may I overcome my hateful rival, evil, and death.
1.6.5.19 He who worships with this indeed overcomes his hateful rival, evil, and death.
1.6.5.20 Now, he worships silently day after day for a year.
1.6.5.21 After the year has passed, whatever desire he may wish for, that he invokes. 1.6.5.22 Truly, that desire falls to his lot who worships with this [rite].

1.6.5.23 This is its Brāhmaṇa: "Verily, he who, having brought [something] day after day for a man, then asks him for it—he indeed approaches him with hostility. 1.6.5.24 Then [the thought arises]: "Who will ask the gods day after day?
This concludes the *Agnyupasthāna*.
